testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What is black ice?
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. You can see the road through it. It looks like a wet road. Watch for black ice when the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: When you approach a vehicle before inspection, you should look under it to:

options.text: Check if the vehicle is on a slope.
Check for fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
Check if the vehicle is in a parking spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
questions.explanation: Before inspecting your vehicle, look under it for fresh leaks of oil, grease, or fuel. Also check around the vehicle for hazards like people, other vehicles, or low branches.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning light comes on while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and park where you are.
Leave the roadway as soon as safely possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the roadway as soon as safely possible.
questions.explanation: If the low pressure warning light comes on while driving, safely leave the roadway as soon as possible and park. Low air pressure means your brakes will not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: When loading cargo, it is important to:

options.text: Stack items as high as possible.
Know the weight limit of the suspension system.
Put light items under heavy items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know the weight limit of the suspension system.
questions.explanation: You must make sure your vehicle is not overloaded. Know the legal weight limits and the maximum weight your vehicle can carry, including the suspension system limit.

questions.question: A thin layer of ice on road surfaces is called:
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road surface through it. A road with black ice may look wet. Be careful when temperatures are below freezing and roads look wet.

questions.question: When an S-cam turns inside a brake drum, it:

options.text: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
Presses the brake shoes against the brake linings.
Presses the brake linings against the wheel axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, the S-cam turns and pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This friction slows the vehicle.

questions.question: If an intersection has two left turn lanes, which should you use?
questions.explanation: You may need to swing right before turning left. When two left turn lanes are available, always start your turn in the rightmost lane.

questions.question: Dry bulk tanks usually have:
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks have high centers of gravity, so they require careful driving. Be ready for the cargo to shift during travel.

questions.question: An alcohol evaporator in an air brake system:

options.text: Stops ice from forming in the brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops ice from forming in the brake system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an evaporator that adds alcohol to the system. This alcohol helps prevent ice from forming inside the brakes.

questions.question: Placards for hazardous cargo must be placed:

options.text: Only on the front of the vehicle.
On the front, back, and sides of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front, back, and sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Placards must be on the front, back, and both sides of a vehicle carrying hazardous cargo. They must be readable from any direction.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle controls skills test, where should your vehicle's final position be?

options.text: In the general area the examiner described.
In the exact position the examiner described.
Within three feet of the position the examiner described.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the exact position the examiner described.
questions.explanation: You must finish each exercise with your vehicle in the exact position the examiner described. If you do not complete an exercise exactly as described, you may fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: What should a driver ensure about the truck?

options.text: The cargo is mostly in the front of the trailer.

questions.explanation: Safe operation of a truck requires proper loading of cargo. Improper loading can damage the vehicle and affect how it handles. Loose cargo can also fall and cause serious injury or death.

questions.question: How many hours of sleep does an adult need each day to stay alert?
questions.explanation: Getting enough sleep is essential for safe driving. Most adults need eight to nine hours of sleep each night to stay alert and focused while driving.

questions.question: What should be done about broken suspension parts?

options.text: They should be repaired, but not right away.

questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle and its load while keeping the axles in place. A broken suspension is extremely dangerous and must be fixed right away.

questions.question: Is emergency equipment required in a vehicle?

options.text: Only for vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: Before each trip, check for required emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one working fire extinguisher.

questions.question: If you see an aggressive driver get into a crash ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and yell at them.
Stop a safe distance away and tell police what you saw.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop a safe distance away and tell police what you saw.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash involving an aggressive driver, stop at a safe distance from the scene. Wait for police and tell them about the aggressive behavior you witnessed.

questions.question: When are you most likely to encounter strong winds?
questions.explanation: Strong winds can push your vehicle out of its lane. This is especially dangerous when coming out of a tunnel.

questions.question: How should a truck be parked?

options.text: So it must be backed up to leave.
So it can be pulled forward to leave.

questions.correctAnswerText: So it can be pulled forward to leave.
questions.explanation: Backing is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Avoid backing whenever possible. Choose parking spaces where you can pull forward when leaving.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, what should you do?

options.text: Try to stay in their way.

questions.explanation: When facing an aggressive driver, get out of their way if you can. Do not make eye contact, as this may make them more angry. Ignore any gestures they make.

questions.question: What should you do when driving down a steep hill?

options.text: Put the vehicle in low gear and use engine braking.
Continuously downshift instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the vehicle in low gear and use engine braking.
questions.explanation: On long or steep hills, use engine braking to control your speed. Use your brakes only to help the engine braking.

questions.question: When should you slow down for a curve?
questions.explanation: Slow down to a safe speed before entering a curve. Slowing down while in the curve can cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, what happens if one air system has low pressure?

options.text: None of the brakes will work.
Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
There is usually no noticeable effect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully if one air system has low pressure. If this happens while driving, exit the road and park as soon as possible.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, how does stopping distance change?

options.text: It is longer than on a regular driving surface.
It is shorter than on a regular driving surface.
It is about the same as on a regular driving surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is longer than on a regular driving surface.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance is longer on slippery surfaces because your tires have less grip on the road.

questions.question: When it is hard to see, like at dawn or dusk, how can you increase your vehicle's visibility?

options.text: Flash your lights on and off.

questions.explanation: Use your headlights on low beam during dawn, dusk, or bad weather to increase your visibility to other drivers.

questions.question: How should you do a pre-trip vehicle inspection?
questions.explanation: Always do your pre-trip inspection the same way. This helps you remember all the steps and makes sure you do not forget to check anything.

questions.question: If your vehicle catches fire, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Park away from buildings, trees, brush, and other vehicles.
Call emergency services and tell them where you are.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, pull off the road into an open area. Do not go to a service station because the fuel there could catch fire. Call emergency services and tell them your location.

questions.question: Can a smaller vehicle stop faster than a larger vehicle?

options.text: Yes, usually it will stop faster.
No, it will take more time to stop.
No, it will take about the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, usually it will stop faster.
questions.explanation: A smaller vehicle can usually stop faster than a larger vehicle. Keep this in mind when deciding how far back to follow another vehicle.

questions.question: When making an emergency stop, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve your trailer to the right and stop.
Swerve your trailer to the left and stop.

questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, keep your vehicle in a straight line. You can use controlled or stab braking. Stopping straight helps you stay safe and lets you turn if you need to.

questions.question: When alley docking, what should you do first?

options.text: Position your vehicle directly in front of the alley.
Back up directly in front of the alley.
Stop parallel to the outer boundary of the alley.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop parallel to the outer boundary of the alley.
questions.explanation: For alley docking, drive past the alley first. Stop your vehicle parallel to the outer boundary. Then back into the alley parking area in a straight line.

questions.question: When asked to change lanes during the driving test, what should you do?

options.text: Change lanes right away without looking.
Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
Change lanes as fast as possible, even if it means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
questions.explanation: When the examiner asks you to change lanes, check for traffic first. Use your turn signal and change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: If you are not sure you have enough space to drive under a bridge or sign, you should:
questions.explanation: If you are unsure your vehicle will fit under overhead objects, slow down and take a different route if possible.

questions.question: A ____ lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes.
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes. The driver controls it with a lever on the dashboard.

questions.question: In cool weather, when temperature rises and ice starts to melt:

options.text: It is usually safe to drive.

questions.explanation: When temperature rises and ice melts, the road becomes even more slippery. Water from melting sits on top of the ice, reducing grip. Always slow down and drive carefully on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: Hydroplaning usually happens:

options.text: In areas where water collects on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: In areas where water collects on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens on roads with water buildup. It can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph if enough water is present. Hydroplaning is more likely with under-inflated or worn tires.

questions.question: Eating while driving:

options.text: Is a good way to save time.

questions.explanation: Eating while driving is dangerous because it takes your attention away from the road and requires you to take one hand off the steering wheel.

questions.question: Regrooved tires are:

options.text: Allowed only on the front of a bus.
Allowed only on the rear of a bus.
Not allowed anywhere on a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed only on the rear of a bus.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires cannot be used on the front of a bus.

questions.question: A trailer's center of gravity should be:

options.text: At the rear of the trailer.

questions.explanation: Cargo weight should be loaded as low as possible. A center of gravity that is too high increases the risk of rollover.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver crashes on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Stop at a safe distance, wait for police, and tell them what you saw.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at a safe distance, wait for police, and tell them what you saw.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash caused by an aggressive driver, stop at a safe distance from the crash, wait for police, and report the aggressive behavior you witnessed.

questions.question: When driving a 50-foot truck at 50 mph, your minimum following distance should be:
questions.explanation: Below 40 mph, allow one second of distance for every 10 feet of vehicle length. At higher speeds, use the same formula and add one more second.

questions.question: ____ is required emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must carry emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, three reflective triangles (or six fuses or three flares), and at least one fully charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What color light shows that anti-lock brakes are not working?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with anti-lock brakes have a yellow warning light. This light shows there is a problem with the braking system.

questions.question: If you skid from pushing too hard on the accelerator, what should you do?

options.text: Take your foot off the accelerator

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the accelerator
questions.explanation: Remove your foot from the accelerator to stop the skid. This type of skid happens most often on snow or ice.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual air brakes, a leak in one system ____ the second system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other system.

questions.question: How should cargo inside a trailer be handled?

options.text: It does not need to be secured
It should be stacked no more than three feet high
It should be secured to prevent movement

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be secured to prevent movement
questions.explanation: Cargo in a trailer must be secured properly. This prevents it from shifting while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: What happens after two violations for using a hand-held mobile phone while driving?

options.text: You must cancel your mobile phone service
You must drive 10 mph under the speed limit for a period of time

questions.explanation: After two convictions for hand-held mobile phone use while driving, your CDL will be disqualified. Penalties become worse with more violations.

questions.question: What is a danger of swerving to avoid a hazard while driving a large truck?

options.text: The truck may miss the object
The truck may stay in the same lane

questions.explanation: Swerving can be safe, but it has risks. Tall vehicles and tractors with multiple trailers can flip over when swerving.

questions.question: What vehicle should you use when taking a CDL driving test?

options.text: The same type of vehicle you will drive with your CDL
Any type of vehicle, even if it is different from what you will drive
A vehicle supplied by the testing station

questions.correctAnswerText: The same type of vehicle you will drive with your CDL
questions.explanation: You must take the skills test in the type of vehicle you plan to drive. You are usually responsible for providing the test vehicle.

questions.question: When parked on a flat surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use wheel chocks to keep your vehicle from moving
Use wheel chocks only after applying the parking brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Use wheel chocks to keep your vehicle from moving
questions.explanation: Always use wheel chocks when parked on a level surface. This is essential if the vehicle does not have spring brakes.

questions.question: When going downhill, brake until you reach a speed that is:
questions.explanation: Going downhill, brake until your speed is 5 mph below safe speed. Then release the brake. Repeat this process.

questions.question: What does rust around wheel nuts mean?
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may mean they are loose. Check that the nuts are tight if you see rust in this area.
